details.airportInfo: Austin–Bergstrom sits southeast of downtown Austin. The campus is just north of downtown, a short drive or bus ride from the airport.
details.funFact: Cass Gilbert's Battle Hall set the look of the whole campus: its Spanish red tile roof, deep overhanging eaves and limestone walls shaped Paul Cret's 1933 master plan, which new buildings still have to follow today.
details.languageInfo: Campus has its own shorthand: the Main Building is simply 'the Tower', and when it glows orange at night it is celebrating a university victory.
details.transportationFact: The historic core around the Main Building and the South Mall is compact and best explored on foot. Austin's CapMetro buses run along Guadalupe Street on the campus's western edge.

buildings.wiki: Main Building (University of Texas at Austin)
buildings.name: UT Tower
buildings.description: Paul Cret's Beaux-Arts Main Building rises in a 94-metre tower of 27 floors at the very heart of campus, crowned by a 56-bell carillon, the largest in Texas. Since 1937 it has been lit orange to mark the university's big moments.

buildings.name: Battle Hall
buildings.description: Cass Gilbert's 1911 library, with its Spanish red tile roof, overhanging eaves and limestone walls, became the template for the whole campus. Known as 'The Old Library', it now houses the architecture library and the Alexander Architectural Archives.
buildings.address: University of Texas at Austin, Austin, TX 78712

buildings.name: Garrison Hall
buildings.description: Home of the history department, Garrison Hall wears Texas history on its walls: names of heroes of the Texas Revolution are carved into the facade, and 32 historic cattle brands run in order of age beneath the eaves.

buildings.wiki: Texas Science and Natural History Museum
buildings.name: Texas Memorial Museum
buildings.description: Built for the Texas Centennial, this Art Deco museum had its ground broken by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1936 and opened in 1939. John F. Staub designed it, with Paul Cret supervising, and today it is the Texas Science & Natural History Museum.
buildings.architect: John F. Staub (Paul Cret, supervising architect)
buildings.address: University of Texas at Austin, Austin, TX 78712

buildings.name: Littlefield House
buildings.description: This ornate Victorian mansion was built in 1893 for George Littlefield, a Civil War veteran, banker and cattleman who became one of the university's great benefactors. It cost $50,000 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

details.airportInfo: Heathrow lies west of central London. The Piccadilly line runs straight from the airport to Russell Square, a short walk from UCL's Bloomsbury campus.
details.funFact: UCL's main building took 158 years to finish: William Wilkins started it in 1827, the money ran out in 1829 with only the portico and dome complete, and the full U-shaped plan was not finished until 1985.
details.languageInfo: Founded in 1826 as the first university in England open to students of any religion, UCL still gets teased by King's students as the 'Godless' college of Gower Street.
details.transportationFact: The Bloomsbury campus is compact and easy to explore on foot. Euston Square, Warren Street and Goodge Street Underground stations are all on its doorstep.

buildings.name: UCL Main Building
buildings.description: William Wilkins, architect of the National Gallery, gave UCL its grand classical portico and ornate dome facing Gower Street. Beneath the dome, the Octagon and Flaxman Gallery hold John Flaxman's sculpture casts, and the oldest parts of the building are Grade I listed.
buildings.newUse: Main library, Octagon and university offices

buildings.name: Cruciform Building
buildings.description: Alfred Waterhouse's last commission, a red-brick Gothic hospital laid out as a cross, with operating theatres at the centre and airy wards in the wings to keep patients apart. Built for University College Hospital, it now houses UCL's Wolfson Institute and parts of the Medical School.

buildings.name: Institute of Education building
buildings.description: Denys Lasdun, architect of the National Theatre, built this long Grade II* listed concrete block along Bedford Way between 1970 and 1976. Its Brutalist bulk cutting through Bloomsbury's Georgian squares made it one of London's most debated buildings.

buildings.name: Senate House
buildings.description: Next door to UCL, Charles Holden's Portland stone Art Deco tower is the headquarters of the University of London, which UCL belongs to. Its 19 floors rise 64 metres, and George Orwell's Ministry of Truth in Nineteen Eighty-Four is often read as a portrait of it.
buildings.oldUse: University of London headquarters and library
buildings.newUse: University of London headquarters and Senate House Library

details.nickname: Sancte et Sapienter (With Holiness and Wisdom)
details.airportInfo: Heathrow lies west of central London. The Piccadilly line runs from the airport to Holborn, a short walk from the Strand Campus.
details.funFact: When King's was founded, John Nash, the architect of Buckingham Palace, offered to design its first building for free. The college turned him down and hired Sir Robert Smirke instead, because Smirke was already the architect of Somerset House next door.
details.languageInfo: Look out for Reggie the Lion, the students' union mascot: a papier-mâché Reggie stands on the staircase in the King's Building foyer.
details.transportationFact: The Strand Campus sits between the Strand and the Thames, with Temple Underground station just along the river. The Maughan Library on Chancery Lane is an easy walk away.

buildings.name: King's Building
buildings.description: The college's founding building, designed by Sir Robert Smirke, architect of the British Museum, and built between 1829 and 1831 to complete the riverside frontage of Somerset House. Its Grade I listed Great Hall, foyer statues of Sappho and Sophocles, and chapel are still the heart of the Strand Campus.
buildings.newUse: Lecture theatres, Great Hall and offices

buildings.name: Chapel of King's College London
buildings.description: Sir George Gilbert Scott rebuilt Smirke's plain chapel in 1864 as an ancient basilica, perched above the Great Hall and reached by a grand double staircase. The apse glows with a copy of a Salviati mosaic of Christ in Majesty.
buildings.architect: Sir George Gilbert Scott (original by Sir Robert Smirke)

buildings.name: Maughan Library
buildings.description: Once the Public Record Office, the 'strong-box of the Empire', this neo-Gothic archive was built with fireproof cell-like storerooms and no heating. King's bought it in 2001 and turned it into its largest library, with a round reading room under a painted zinc ceiling.

buildings.name: Somerset House
buildings.description: Sir William Chambers' vast neoclassical palace of government offices wraps a 91-metre courtyard on the Strand, with a riverside frontage 150 metres wide. King's College London's own King's Building was built to complete that river front.
